Actinobacterial CofA-family membrane protein (Pfam DUF3566, 2 TM helices). Reported to interact with the transmembrane domain of PonA2 (Rv3682) -- the M. tuberculosis ortholog of Corynebacterium glutamicum PBP1a -- and explicitly NOT with that of PonA1 (Rv0050), the PBP1b ortholog, in a heterologous POLAR two-hybrid assay in E. coli using full-length Mtb CofA as prey; the authors themselves describe this signal as weak, and it is strengthened when the Mtb-specific N-terminal extension (residues 1-190) is deleted (Sher, Lim & Bernhardt 2020, eLife, 10.7554/eLife.54761). CofA is proposed to act as a conserved partner promoting aPBP-mediated peptidoglycan synthesis, paralleling its role with PBP1a in C. glutamicum. Note that one sentence of that paper's Results attributes the CofA-DeltaN gain to PonA1; its own Discussion, its figure-supplement title and its orthology statements all say PonA2, so the partner is reported here as PonA2 only. Genetic support is indirect: Tn-seq shows Mtb CofA becomes less dispensable when the NON-cognate aPBP PonA1 is inactivated, which the primary source reads -- through the known PonA1-PonA2 synthetic lethality -- as consistent with CofA being required for PonA2 function (Kieser et al. 2015, PNAS, PMID 26438867). No physical interaction involving CofA, PonA1 or PonA2 is recorded in curated interaction databases (see evidence). Also consistent with this atlas's own phenotype layer (Tn-seq): altered fitness specifically under meropenem (a PBP/peptidoglycan-synthesis-targeting antibiotic, lfc -5.02) and in mouse infection (day 45, lfc -7.24) -- both noted in this atlas before this literature connection was made. "CofA" is the name used by the primary source but is not yet an official NCBI/UniProt gene symbol for the M. tuberculosis locus; treated here as a functional annotation, not a confirmed nomenclature assignment.

Candidate toxin of a type II toxin-antitoxin module. All-vs-all structural clustering (Foldseek on ESMFold models, phase36) shows a SIGNIFICANT fold match (E=2.4e-4, TM-score 0.77) to Rv2663, the ribosome-dependent ribonuclease toxin of the RelS-RelI system (Han 2026). The immediately adjacent, overlapping gene Rv0123 (intergenic gap -4 bp) is a predicted RHH/copG-type DNA-binding antitoxin, so Rv0122-Rv0123 is a plausible cognate toxin-antitoxin pair. No prior literature describes this locus as a TA system (novel structural prediction). CAVEAT: a shared toxin fold is not proof of ribonuclease activity, and the ESMFold model of Rv0122 is of moderate confidence (pLDDT 59); toxin activity and TA function remain to be validated experimentally.

L,D-transpeptidase 4 (LdtMt4). Generates 3->3 cross-links in peptidoglycan: cleaves the mDap(3)-D-Ala(4) bond of a tetrapeptide donor stem and forms a bond between the carbonyl of mDap(3) of the donor stem and the side chain of mDap(3) of the acceptor stem; specific for tetrapeptide donor stems (UniProt O07436, SwissProt-reviewed, evidence at protein level, EC 2.3.2.-). Experimentally characterised: Cordillot et al. 2013 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 57:5940, PMID 24041897) purified the five M. tuberculosis L,D-transpeptidase paralogues (Mt1 to Mt5) and found Mt4 active both in peptidoglycan cross-linking and in beta-lactam acylation, making it part of the carbapenem-target set. Domain architecture Big_10 (PF17964) + YkuD (PF03734), shared with ldtA/Rv0116c, lprQ/Rv0483, ldtMt3/Rv1433 and ldtB/Rv2518c. RefSeq still labels this locus 'hypothetical protein'.

Confident match (15 independent PDB templates, Probability 97.8-98.5%, E-values 1.5e-6 to 1.7e-9) to a single HKD-type catalytic module of the phospholipase D (PLD) / nuclease-phosphodiesterase superfamily -- convergent hits span mitochondrial cardiolipin synthase, CDP-diacylglycerol--serine O-phosphatidyltransferase, phospholipase D isoforms, and 5'-3' exonucleases PLD3/PLD4, all unified by the shared HKD fold. The aligned region (~90 of 130 residues, corresponding to one lobe of the canonical bipartite PLD fold used by most templates, whose HKD module pairs are 2-8x longer) suggests Rv0396 carries a single HKD module rather than a canonical two-lobed phospholipase D. The PLD/HKD superfamily is functionally diverse (phospholipases, phosphatidyltransferases, nucleases), so the precise catalytic activity in M. tuberculosis is undetermined from fold alone.

Circularly permuted NlpC/P60 (YaeF/YiiX-family) cysteine amidase with a structurally competent Cys234-His97 catalytic dyad (Glu115 a candidate third member). RefSeq leaves this locus 'hypothetical protein'; here it is re-annotated by structure-guided active-site mapping. The catalytic histidine partner of the nucleophile Cys234 is His97 (Sgamma-Ndelta1 = 3.6 A on the ESMFold model, 2.9 A on AlphaFold3), invisible to sequence proximity because the fold is circularly permuted - the three sequence-proximal histidines lie 7-23 A away. HHpred matches the permuted Peptidase_C92 / YaeF-YiiX family (>=99.7%) and lipid-acting permuted members (LRAT, H-REV107), and the 86%-hydrophobic pocket points to an N-acyl-amino-acid / lipoprotein amide substrate rather than a peptidoglycan muropeptide. Distinct from the five canonical peptidoglycan-hydrolase NlpC/P60 enzymes of H37Rv (Rv0024, RipA, RipB, RipD, Rv2190c). Catalytic codons essentially invariant across ~250,724 MTBC genomes. A structural prediction, not a biochemical assay.

WS/DGAT domain-containing protein. Pfam: WS_DGAT_C (PF06974.19, residues 270-413, 34.4 bits vs GA 20.7). The CATALYTIC domain of the family (PF03007, WS_DGAT_cat) is not annotated by UniProt but is not absent either: an unthresholded hmmsearch scores it at 15.7 bits over residues 8-168, below the 23.6-bit gathering threshold, against 276.4 bits for tgs1/Rv3130c and no hit at all for the neighbouring ephC/Rv1124 (mtbc/Rv1125, piste P8, 2026-09-06). The HHxxxDG motif (137-143) lies in this sub-threshold catalytic region, not in the annotated C-terminal domain. Unrestricted Foldseek search (AFDB-swissprot) confirms WS/DGAT as the best absolute structural match (top hits: MTBC Tgs/DGAT paralogs TM=0.71-0.79, and A. baylyi WSD Q8GGG1 TM=0.73), not merely the only candidate tested. ESM-1v masked-marginal LLR (Meier et al. 2021) on the aligned catalytic dyad shows a residue-level gradient: His138/Asp142 (matching the conserved WS/DGAT catalytic pair H133/D137, the more critical residue per Stoveken et al. 2009) fall in the 90-100th percentile of evolutionary constraint against a 20-point background scan, while Ala137 (the position of the lost first histidine) sits near the background median (60-65th percentile). CORRECTION 2026-09-06 (mtbc/Rv1125, piste P10): the glycine of the HHxxxDG motif is Gly143, not Ser147 -- the motif is contiguous (residues 137-143 read A-H-A-L-G-D-G), and the 147 pairing came from the 14%-identity structural alignment to 7NXG, which inserts a 4-residue gap between the D and the G that none of the 12 MTBC paralogs shows. Gly143 is conserved and constrained (ESM-1v LLR -8.4 for G143S, 83rd percentile), so Rv1125 retains three of the four motif positions and has lost only the first histidine. CAVEAT (solvent-accessibility follow-up, Bio.PDB.SASA on the local AlphaFold model): all 4 catalytic/motif positions are buried (RSA 0.009-0.233, Gly143 marginally), as are the two most-constrained background positions (D10, Y405) -- burial alone explains much of the ESM-1v signal, so the gradient is consistent with EITHER a modified-but-real catalytic site OR generic structural/folding importance; ESM-1v and RSA together do not distinguish the two. Not proof of activity -- only a direct enzymatic assay could settle it. Source: mtbc/Rv1125 project, piste P1.3.f/P1.5.a/P1.5.b. UPDATE (mtbc/Rv1125 project, pistes P1.6-P1.8, 2026-09-01-02): comparison to the 12 other experimentally characterized MTBC Tgs/DGAT paralogs shows the loss of the first catalytic histidine (Ala137 replacing His132 of the canonical HHxxxDG motif) is not unique to Rv1125 -- one paralog, Rv2484c (itself the least active gene of the Daniel et al. 2004 screen), independently shares it. Cross-species polarization by targeted tblastn against 8 NTM/MTBAP/Corynebacteriales orthologs (up to 69% identity, far above the 14% of the only prior structural template) shows 7 of 8 orthologs retain the same alanine, including two of three genomes entirely outside genus Mycobacterium (Gordonia bronchialis, Tsukamurella paurometabola; the sole exception, Mycobacteroides abscessus, carries a serine, a further independent substitution rather than a reversion) -- while His138, Asp142 and Gly143 are conserved without exception in all 8. This places the loss of the first catalytic histidine at or before the divergence of Corynebacteriales, at least 200 million years ago: not a recent, Rv1125-specific degeneration, but the ancestral state of an entire structural lineage. Six independent computational methods across two registers (structural/evolutionary modelling: ESM-1v, RSA/SASA, Boltz-2 docking, paralog comparison, McDonald-Kreitman with M. canettii outgroup; and cross-species orthology) all leave catalytic specificity open rather than resolving it -- only direct enzymatic or mutagenesis data could settle whether this is a genuine but mechanistically distinct acyltransferase or an enzyme losing its catalytic function. SEPARATELY, this gene appeared as a candidate in a doctoral-thesis GWAS of tuberculosis clinical form (pulmonary vs meningeal; La PhD thesis 2023), whose candidates concentrate in lipid-biosynthesis pathways. Its only common variation in the complex is 3 linked SNPs (NC_000962.3:1248936/1248382/1248978), and re-genotyping all 142,694 genomes of the group's curated database shows these are EXACT CLADE MARKERS with no within-lineage variation anywhere: ~100% in lineages 1, 2, 3, 5-9 and the animal lineages, 1/54,539 and 0/54,539 in lineage 4 for the first two, and 82.65% for the third in lineage 4, resolving entirely at the sub-lineage partition (0% in L4.8 and L4.9, ~100% elsewhere). Their ancestral state is corroborated in M. canettii (95-96% of 153 genomes). A mono-locus association is therefore not identifiable at this locus: the variation IS clade membership. Source: mtbc/Rv1125 project, pistes P1.6-P1.8/P3/P7, manuscript in preparation. At 86 aa it is a minimal single-domain SAS, DISTINCT from the main bifunctional Rel(Mtb)/Rv2583c (738 aa). The FaRel2/ATfaRel2 (toxSAS) hits raise the possibility of a toxic small-alarmone-synthetase (toxSAS; TA / phage-defence) rather than a canonical (p)ppGpp synthetase; the neighbouring hypothetical Rv1366 (STRING 834) is a candidate cognate partner. Subtype (synthetase vs toxSAS) undetermined. CONTEXT (twin-synthetase landscape, Sinha 2023): M. tuberculosis has two characterised bifunctional synthetases - Rel(Rv2583c) and the RNase-HII-fused short SAS RelZ (~500 aa); at 86 aa Rv1366A matches NEITHER (too short for RelZ), so it is a candidate ADDITIONAL monofunctional small/toxic alarmone synthetase, not yet experimentally characterised.

EST12 (early secreted target, 12 kDa), a secreted effector encoded in region-of-difference RD3. RefSeq leaves it 'hypothetical'. Secreted EST12 binds the receptor for activated C kinase 1 (RACK1) and recruits the deubiquitinase UCHL5 to deubiquitinate NLRP3, triggering NLRP3-caspase-1-gasdermin-D pyroptosis and IL-1beta release; it also regulates Myc via RACK1-JNK-AP1. A crystal structure identifies Y80 as the RACK1-binding residue; ΔEST12 is more susceptible in vitro and in vivo (Qu 2020). No Sec/Tat signal peptide is predicted for EST12 (DeepTMHMM, this atlas), and that does not contradict its secretion: the same layer also calls the canonical ESX substrates ESAT-6 (Rv3875) and CFP-10 (Rv3874) globular, so if this protein is exported it is by a route that leaves no recognisable signal.

Putative nuclease: our own domain scan finds only the DUF222 domain (Pfam PF02720, 'domain of unknown function'); the 'HNH' label comes from COG1403 orthology, not an independent hit. No catalytic site verified (no M-CSA match), cleavage target undetermined, and our structural layer returns no match at all for this protein (no hit above threshold). Small, densely helical membrane folds are a documented cross-matching pitfall in this programme (cf. the TM-helix promiscuity artefact already flagged on other dark genes); the E-value here is markedly stronger than that pattern's usual noise range, but in the absence of any genetic corroboration this is read as a FOLD assignment (small MerF-like membrane protein family), not a functional one.

Conserved hypothetical protein of 149 aa whose single domain, DUF6941 (PF22091, residues 5-130), belongs to Pfam clan CL0159 (E-set, immunoglobulin-like fold). Function unknown. What is established is an architectural oddity rather than an activity: in H37Rv every other cytoplasmic E-set domain is an accessory module inside a large enzyme (366-1215 aa: bglS, alpha-mannosidase, ceramidase, glgE, glgP, malQ, pepN), whereas here the Ig-like domain is the entire protein, and Pfam describes DUF6941 itself as a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins sharing similarity with the Ig-like modules of xylosyltransferases, alkylpurine DNA glycosylases and cycloisomaltooligosaccharide glucanotransferases. The domain leaves no N-terminal room for a signal peptide, so the predicted cytoplasmic localisation is constrained by the architecture and not only by DeepTMHMM - which makes the nearest structural analogues found by Foldseek (RbmA, the Vibrio cholerae biofilm scaffolding protein; complement C3) informative as folds but misleading as compartments, both being extracellular adhesion/matrix Ig-folds. No paralogue carries DUF6941 elsewhere in H37Rv. Non-essential (NE), not vulnerable (CRISPRi VI +1.56), genus-restricted (deepest homolog within Mycobacterium), and never mentioned in the literature.

Macrodomain protein (Pfam Macro, PF01661.28, residues 193-302, i-E 1.4e-29). The inherited product name «lipoprotein LppD» is not supported by this atlas: on the 343-residue RefSeq form served here (NP_216415.1), neither DeepTMHMM nor the Kyte-Doolittle/lipobox second opinion finds a signal peptide or a lipobox, where the same layer recovers the lipobox of the four acylated lipoproteins used as controls (LprG, LpqH, Mpt83, LprA). Of the 92 loci of the atlas that carry such an inherited name, 86 have a predicted export signal (58 of them a lipobox) and 4 more are predicted to sit in the membrane; this locus and Rv1946c are the only two with neither. Two protein forms are on record for this locus, and they are not equivalent for this question: UniProt P9WK29 has 359 residues, the RefSeq form plus a 16-residue N-terminal extension (MAAMRAHARRRHPHAL) whose arginine/histidine-rich stretch is exactly the charged n-region a signal peptide requires. The discrepancy, and the unresolved signal-peptide question behind it, were already raised by Lai et al. 2012 (PLoS ONE, 10.1371/journal.pone.0035018), who also review the contradictory experimental record: the protein has been reported both in a membrane fraction and in an 'exported lipoprotein' 2-DE/MS analysis, and a candidate O-glycosylation was tested and not confirmed. Those primary sources are reported as cited there, not verified here. The only primary study of the protein itself (Menon et al. 2025, Int J Mol Sci, 10.3390/ijms262210872) treats it as a macrodomain that interacts with host HDAC1-ZBTB25 and promotes stress resistance and immune evasion in infected macrophages, and does not address its localisation. Detected in 15 of 16 PaxDb datasets (227 ppm, 77.7th percentile).

Secreted immunomodulatory protein with intrinsically disordered regions and B/T-cell epitopes. Treatment of macrophages with recombinant Rv1954A triggers TLR4-mediated activation with increased IL-12 and TNF-alpha secretion, and upregulates CD80/CD86/CD40/MHC I-II, consistent with a role in enhancing antigen presentation. A Rv1954A knock-in M. smegmatis strain (Ms_Rv1954A) shows increased macrophage infectivity, induces ROS/RNS, and Rv1954A itself protects against oxidative/nitrosative stress, enhancing intracellular survival. Mice immunized with Ms_Rv1954A mount a Th1 response; intratracheal infection causes lymphocyte infiltration without granuloma formation. Rv1954A is immunogenic (elevated IgG titres in PTB patients vs controls), suggesting utility as a diagnostic marker (Arora et al. 2020, Front Cell Infect Microbiol, DOI 10.3389/fcimb.2020.564565). Single-study origin, not yet independently replicated -- confidence kept at medium rather than high. No Sec/Tat signal peptide and no transmembrane helix are predicted here (DeepTMHMM, confirmed by this atlas' Kyte-Doolittle second opinion); the same layer also calls the canonical ESX substrates ESAT-6 (Rv3875) and CFP-10 (Rv3874) globular, so if this protein is exported it is by a route that leaves no recognisable signal.

HicA-family toxin (TASmania candidate T144), the toxic component of a functional type II toxin-antitoxin system with Rv2017 as its cognate antitoxin (TASmania candidate A32, Pfam HTH_3). Directly validated by Akarsu et al. 2019 (TASmania, PLoS Comput Biol, PMID 31022176): among 11 in silico TA candidates selected for wet-lab testing (out of >2 million candidates mined genome-wide), Rv2016 was one of only 4 showing 'robust toxicity' upon heterologous expression in M. smegmatis, and a co-expression rescue assay (their Fig. 6) showed that Rv2017 suppresses Rv2016 toxicity -- direct mechanistic confirmation of the toxin-antitoxin pairing, not mere operon co-annotation. Consistent with this atlas's own prior data: Rv2016-Rv2017 form a real 2-gene operon (toxin-then-antitoxin gene order, matching TASmania's reported T->A orientation), and the regulation layer already shows Rv2017 represses Rv2016 -- the expected autoregulation of a TA operon by its antitoxin. No Pfam domain reaches this atlas's own --cut_ga gathering threshold on Rv2016, but HicA domains are short (~50 aa) and often fall below strict Pfam GA cutoffs; TASmania uses a curated HMM pipeline dedicated to TA-system detection rather than a general Pfam scan, so this is not a contradiction.

Confident, near full-length match (95 of 99 residues, Aligned_cols=95) to the WXG100/ESAT-6-like fold: a direct hit to the M. tuberculosis-specific antigen MTB48 (PDB 4WJ1_A, Probability 99.1%, E=1e-9, Score=78.2), followed by a dense cascade of 19 further ESAT-6-like / PE-family / ESX-1 secretion-associated templates at Probability 97.3-98.9% (E=2.9e-8 to 1.1e-4) -- the same reference set already confirmed for the paralogous cases Rv1951c/Rv2077c/Rv2541 (this project, same HHpred programme). Confident fold/family assignment: a small WXG100-fold, ESX/T7SS-associated helical-hairpin protein. Independently corroborated (not used to build this verdict) by this fiche's own pre-existing Foldseek hit, 6uuj-assembly2_E (PE5-PPE4-EspG3 complex from the type VII secretion system, TM=0.69), flagged non-significant at the atlas's structural threshold but thematically convergent with the ESX/T7SS assignment from HHpred. The precise ESX system and cognate EsxB-like partner are not established from fold alone.

N-terminal ~100 residues (of 323) match the WXG100/ESAT-6-like fold (T7SS/ESX-secretion-associated helical hairpin): a strong convergent cascade of 15 independent PDB templates at Probability 97.0-97.8% and E-values 0.00095-0.045, drawing on essentially the same EsxA/EsxB/PE-family reference set flagged as a weaker signal on the paralogous case Rv2541 (P7.1g-lot1, this same lot). Confident fold assignment for the N-terminal module; the remaining ~220 C-terminal residues are unmatched by any template and no cognate ESX secretion-system partner or synteny support has been checked here. Not asserted as a canonical small EsxA-type effector -- 323 aa is atypically large for this fold family, which normally caps near 100 aa.

Three-domain architecture, resolved by domain-wise HHpred and physically justified by inter-domain PAE (not sequence guesswork alone): unit A (aa 1-87, ferredoxin-like fold, Pfam DUF8830/PF31169, restricted to actinomycetes), unit B (aa 88-147, winged helix-turn-helix of the AlpA / excisionase / recombination-directionality-factor family, Pfam PF05930/COG3311), a disordered linker (aa 148-177, median pLDDT 32), and unit C (aa 178-267, immunoglobulin-like beta-sandwich, no assignable family). Isolated on its own, unit B gives HHpred Probability 99.3%, E=1.3e-10 for the AlpA family (best template 8C3T, Wen et al. 2022 NAR) -- a >4500-fold gain in E-value over the same search run on the full-length protein (Probability 98.6-98.64%, E=4e-07/5.9e-7 across two independent HHpred runs) -- which resolves, in favour of DNA binding, the two earlier and mutually contradictory leads this fiche used to carry (a sub-threshold Pfam Sigma70_r4 hit plus a canonical HTH motif at the same residues, versus circular-permutant ribosomal-S6 Foldseek hits): the S6, Sigma70_r4 and Lrp/AsnC framings are now excluded. Unit B is also the single most conserved segment of the protein across the genus (83.8% identity over four independent NTM lineages, against 67.2% for unit C, 55.1% for unit A, 47.2% for the linker), consistent with it carrying the strongest functional constraint. ANTI-OVERCLAIM: this assigns a FOLD AND FAMILY, not a demonstrated activity -- no excisionase/antitermination activity, no operator, and no base-specific DNA contact have been shown for Rv2516c itself; the sequence specificity of any DNA binding remains open after an exhausted computational route (five converging but individually non-significant leads, and two independent Boltz-2 co-folding tests that failed as a DISCRIMINANT METHOD, not as a biological negative). Co-transcribed with Rv2517c in an ancient six-gene cassette (Rv2512c-Rv2517c) entirely deleted, not point-pseudogenized, in M. leprae. Induced by general antibiotic stress, not specifically by DNA damage or the DosR dormancy program (excluded genome-wide). Full dossier: companion project mtbc/Rv2516c/ (iteration 20).

The aligned region (58-68 of 83 residues) matches the compact HicA catalytic module closely in size. No cognate HicB-type antitoxin partner or genomic-context corroboration is asserted here (out of scope for this curation pass); the family/fold assignment stands on the structural evidence alone. Independent of, and not previously flagged by, the literature note already on this fiche (P18.17, an over-interpreted SOS-response summary, corrected 2026-08-10) -- the two observations are unrelated.

Cofactor-independent ABM (antibiotic-biosynthesis-monooxygenase) of the quinone-monooxygenase family (ActVA-Orf6/SnoaB/YgiN), substrate unknown (weaker candidate). RefSeq leaves it 'hypothetical protein'. Tandem-ABM protein (paralogue Rv2557, 69% identity); only the C-terminal lobe forms a competent pocket, centred on His124 and lined by Phe168/Tyr154 - the signature of a cofactorless ABM site where an aromatic substrate replaces flavin. A heme-oxygenase assignment is excluded structurally (geometry not heme-compatible; IsdG/MhuD catalytic determinants absent) and by the fold-paralogue safeguard (heme degradation in M. tuberculosis is already carried by MhuD/Rv3592). HHpred top hits (>=99.9%) are cofactorless ActVA-Orf6/YgiN-family monooxygenases; the IsdG/MhuD heme-oxygenase subfamily is absent. The C-terminal site residues are near-invariant across ~250,724 genomes. Fold and sub-type are well supported; substrate and activity remain undemonstrated.

No molecular function is established, and the verdict stays dark. What the evidence supports is a STATUS, not a function: a small (66 aa), highly abundant protein (733 ppm, 91.5th percentile, detected in 14 of 16 PaxDb datasets) that reaches the extracytoplasmic space and is seen by the immune system. (i) Peptides derived from Rv3196A are presented on MHC class I during infection (Sher et al., eLife 2023, 10.7554/elife.84070, Discussion). (ii) The M. marinum ortholog MMAR_1367 (UniProt B2HFI1, 84.2% identity) is quantified in the SECRETED protein fraction of every one of the 13 deletion-mutant-versus-wild-type comparisons of the ESX-1 proteo-genetic survey of Cronin et al. (PNAS 2022, 10.1073/pnas.2123100119, Dataset S2 -- table row read here, not merely cited), and its secretion is NOT ESX-1-dependent (log2 fold change -0.11 to +0.80, average P >= 0.46, the authors' own threshold never met, including in the deltaeccCb1, deltaesxA and deltaesxB strains). (iii) Rv3196A itself is reported as detected by MS in M. tuberculosis culture filtrates (Bell et al. 2012, 10.1021/pr2007939); that statement is cited by Sher et al. and could NOT be verified here (closed access, no preprint, supplementary tables unreachable). The protein carries no signal peptide and no transmembrane helix (DeepTMHMM, this atlas), so if it is exported it is by a route that leaves no recognisable signal -- which is precisely the reading Sher et al. propose. No Pfam domain, no confident HHpred hit (best E = 8.4, incoherent cohort), no active-site match, singleton operon. Transcriptionally it is strongly inducible: log2 fold change +3.76 in an alkX (rv3249c) deletion mutant, the second highest of the 41 upregulated genes (adjusted P = 1.77e-30; Microbiol Spectrum 2022, 10.1128/spectrum.01969-22, Table 1), and 1.51-fold (pH 5.7) / 1.57-fold (pH 7.0) at 5% versus 0.5% CO2 (Infect Immun 2025, 10.1128/iai.00568-24, Table 1). Read together: an antigenic protein of unknown molecular function, plausibly but not demonstrably exported. Antigenicity and export are a status; neither is a molecular function, and neither requalifies this gene.

Essential (Tn-seq ES, DeJesus et al. 2017; robust to a dedicated read-mappability test) and intrinsically disordered (44.8% disordered residues by metapredict v3 + AlphaFold pLDDT, two IDRs) protein of 183 aa. Physically positioned between sigH (Rv3223c) and rshA (Rv3221A) -- it overlaps both by 4 bp on each side, and has no promoter of its own, being transcribed from the sigH promoter -- but this physical position is NOT equivalent to membership of the SigH regulon or of a functionally demonstrated SigH-RshA operon: Rv3222c is absent from both published SigH regulon definitions (Sharp et al. 2016; Mehra & Kaushal 2009), and the sigH-rshA-Rv3222c operon structure itself is only PREDICTED, never functionally demonstrated to include this gene. Rv3222c is the last coding survivor of a small paralogous gene family degraded by a single ancestral insertion of an IS110-family mobile element (Pfam PF01548): three additional copies survive in H37Rv only as non-coding decayed relics (one disrupted mid-CDS by the insertion itself), and the gene shows stronger purifying selection than these relics. No detectable homology for the protein itself (HHpred no confident hit, Pfam hmmscan --cut_ga 0 hit, Foldseek 0 hit against the full AlphaFold/PDB databases, absent from the ESM Atlas). The previously reported CRISPRi vulnerability index (-15.5) is UNRELIABLE for this gene and should not be cited as a vulnerability claim: Bosch et al. 2021 flag it certain=False/crispr_ess=NonEssential, and its 14 guides are amongst the weakest in the genome (best guide strength 0.430 vs a genome median of 0.960 for the per-gene maximum) -- the underlying model never observed this gene under strong depletion, so the score is an out-of-domain extrapolation, not a measurement. Not previously functionally characterised in the literature: full-text search finds only two pre-2025 mentions of the locus tag, both traceable to a single 2007 locus-tag error (Thakur et al. 2007, JBC) that mislabelled Rv3222c as the anti-sigma factor of SigH, an error the real anti-sigma factor RshA/Rv3221A already carries; UniProt and the core SigH-regulon literature are unaffected. Epoxide hydrolase EphH (EC 3.3.2.10; UniProt O53388, reviewed, protein_existence = '1: Evidence at protein level'). Catalyzes the hydrolysis of epoxide-containing substrates (PubMed:36777032). In vitro, catalyzes the hydrolysis of the synthetic compounds PHOME and styrene oxide (PubMed:36777032). Plays an essential role in subverting phagosomal acidification (PubMed:36777032). Plays a major role in the survival of M. tuberculosis (Mtb) during in vitro acidic stress and protects Mtb in response to phagosomal acidification inside macrophages (PubMed:36777032). Also supports Mtb growth under nutrient-deprived conditions at pH 7.0 (PubMed:36777032). Activity confirmed by enzymatic assay after CRISPRi knockdown, not inferred from domain homology alone (Garg et al. 2022, Front Microbiol, PMID 36777032).

MfpC, a DUF742-family (PF05331.18) protein and guanine-nucleotide exchange factor (GEF) for the small GTPase MfpB (Rv3362c), within the mfpA-mfpB-mfpC-mfpD-mfpE fluoroquinolone-resistance operon (Rv3361c-Rv3365c). This atlas's own Pfam gathering-threshold domain for Rv3363c is DUF742 (i-E=2.6e-36, residues 10-122 of 122, covering nearly the whole protein) -- directly CONTRADICTING the previous function_revised text ('MarR-family DNA-binding transcriptional regulator', from an eggNOG COG1846 category call never reconciled with the atlas's own Pfam layer). Directly named in Cui et al. 2022 (mBio, PMID 36453945, full text: 'The third gene, Rv3363c, encodes MfpC, a protein of 122 amino acids belonging to the DUF742 family') and biochemically characterized in Ye et al. 2024 (PMID 39179666, M. smegmatis MfpC): guanine nucleotide exchange assays and site-directed mutagenesis show MfpC acts as a GEF that regulates MfpB, itself influencing MfpA (a pentapeptide-repeat protein protecting DNA gyrase) at the translational level -- part of the mechanism controlling fluoroquinolone susceptibility. Fully consistent with this atlas's own operon layout: Rv3361c=mfpA (already requalified), Rv3362c='ATP/GTP-binding protein' (=MfpB, the GTPase), Rv3364c='Roadblock LC7' (=MfpD, MfpB's GAP per PMID 36453945), Rv3365c='Histidine kinase' (=MfpE).

No publication mentions this gene under its locus tag or any known ortholog alias.

Candidate accessory of the cholesterol-catabolism module and, more specifically, a candidate ferredoxin / iron-sulfur electron-transfer partner of the KshAB 3-ketosteroid 9alpha-hydroxylase. Rv3527 is the immediate genomic neighbour of kshA (Rv3526), co-occurs phylogenetically with the KstR1 ring-degradation regulon, and is under purifying selection on 145,209 MTBC genomes (6 segregating sites; a real, conserved gene). Structure-based refinement: of its 25 nearest ESM-Atlas neighbours, 11 are annotated as ferredoxins, and the protein carries a Cys78-x-x-Cys81 motif plus distal cysteines (Cys38/Cys107/Cys126) compatible with an Fe-S cluster. Because KshA is a Rieske [2Fe-2S] monooxygenase that depends on electron transfer, an electron-transfer ferredoxin role is mechanistically coherent. A guilt-by-association plus structural-homology hypothesis; the molecular function (electron transfer to KshAB) remains experimentally undemonstrated, so the verdict is kept 'dark'. Decisive test: co-folding Rv3527 with KshA/KshB (AlphaFold-multimer).

Candidate accessory component of the cholesterol-catabolism module, coupled to the 3-ketosteroid 9alpha-hydroxylase sub-module (KshB, Rv3571). Rv3572 is the immediate genomic neighbour of kshB on H37Rv and is phylogenetically and contextually associated (STRING context-driven, text-mining excluded) with kshB and the ring-degradation core (hsaB, hsaD, hsaC, hsaA). It is under purifying selection on 145,209 MTBC genomes (3 synonymous / 4 missense segregating sites; a real, conserved gene). No dedicated functional study of Rv3572 exists in the published TB literature. The association to the cholesterol module is strong; the specific molecular role of the accessory remains undemonstrated (a guilt-by-association hypothesis, not a biochemical assignment).

Binuclear metallo-beta-lactamase (MBL)-fold metallo-hydrolase of the UPF0173/UlaG family (InterPro IPR050114), substrate unassigned. RefSeq leaves it 'hypothetical protein'. The MBL HxHxDH motif (His74-His76-Asp78-His79) was confirmed as a genuine two-metal centre by co-folding the chain with two metal ions on AlphaFold Server (independent Zn and Fe jobs, top model iPTM 0.98): the ions bind a single bridged binuclear site 3.2-3.4 A apart, partitioned into a three-histidine metal (His74/His76/His137) and an aspartate-plus-two-histidine metal (Asp78/His79/His235), with identical geometry for Zn or Fe. HHpred top hits (>=99.8%) are UPF0173/UlaG metal-dependent hydrolases (UlaG 2wyl; COG2220). The fold-paralogue safeguard withholds the RNase Z (held by Rv2407) and glyoxalase II (Rv0634c/Rv2581c) labels: only the fold-level family is claimed. The six metal ligands are effectively invariant across ~250,724 genomes (most frequent non-synonymous ligand variant 0.0032%). A structural prediction, not a biochemical assay.

Heme-homeostasis regulator: the principal driver of the Rv3839-Rv3840 operon that down-regulates endogenous heme biosynthesis under nitric-oxide and iron-limitation stress (Quirk 2026). It carries a DUF2470/DRI (Domain Related to Iron) regulatory module - the GluTR-binding-protein domain, also found in HugZ - and lies immediately upstream of bacterioferritin bfrB (Rv3841), in an operon with the transcriptional regulator Rv3840. The fold-paralogue safeguard is passed: it is not a copy of the genuine glutamyl-tRNA reductase HemA/Rv0509 but shares only the regulatory DUF2470 domain. RefSeq left this locus uncharacterised; the structure-guided hypothesis (heme/iron homeostasis) was confirmed experimentally by Quirk 2026 while the companion study was in progress - a RefSeq-behind case and an independent validation of the approach.

Secreted protein (found in culture filtrate), conserved across mycobacteria, with an X-ray crystal structure of fragment 184-410 that defines a new protein family (an alpha/beta/alpha sandwich + alpha-helix bundle; no structures for homologues previously known). Immunoglobulin-like, candidate vaccine antigen. Molecular function unknown. (UniProt auto-name 'Tat' is a database artefact and is not adopted.) No Sec/Tat signal peptide is predicted here (DeepTMHMM, this atlas), so the culture-filtrate detection is not explained by a classical export signal: the same layer also calls the canonical ESX substrates ESAT-6 (Rv3875) and CFP-10 (Rv3874) globular, so if this protein is exported it is by a route that leaves no recognisable signal. A culture-filtrate protein can also arrive there by lysis; the detection is compatible with export, it does not prove it.
